score_quality.text:
Classic Banana Bread
Serves 8
Ingredients
3 ripe bananas, mashed
1/3 cup melted butter
1 teaspoon baking soda
Pinch of salt
3/4 cup sugar
1 large egg, beaten
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
Directions
1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees and butter a loaf pan.
2. In a mixing bowl, mash the ripe bananas with a fork until completely smooth.
3. Stir the melted butter into the mashed bananas.
4. Mix in the baking soda and salt. Stir in the sugar, beaten egg, and vanilla extract.
5. Mix in the flour. Pour the batter into your prepared loaf pan.
6. Bake for 55 minutes to one hour, until a tester inserted into the center comes out clean.
7. Remove from oven and let cool in the pan for a few minutes.

Ingredients for a lovely lemonade that the whole family will enjoy on a hot day
1 cup freshly squeezed lemon juice from about six lemons
1 cup granulated white sugar, or a little less to taste
5 cups cold water, divided into one and four cups
Directions for making the syrup and mixing everything together
1. Heat one cup of water with the sugar until dissolved completely
2. Add the lemon juice and the remaining four cups of cold water
3. Chill in the refrigerator for at least one hour before serving
Serve over plenty of ice with a slice of lemon on each glass

score_quality.text:
It was a bright cold day in April and the clocks were striking.
Winston Smith, his chin nuzzled into his breast in an effort to escape
the vile wind, slipped quickly through the glass doors of Victory Mansions,
though not quickly enough to prevent a swirl of gritty dust from entering
along with him. The hallway smelt of boiled cabbage and old rag mats.
At one end of it a coloured poster, too large for indoor display,
had been tacked to the wall. It depicted simply an enormous face,
more than a metre wide: the face of a man of about forty-five,
with a heavy black moustache and ruggedly handsome features.
Winston made for the stairs. It was no use trying the lift.
Even at the best of times it was seldom working.

the flour and the butter and the sugar go into a large mixing bowl

whisk everything together until the batter is smooth and glossy
pour the batter into a buttered tin and bake it in a moderate oven

leave it to cool on a rack before turning it out onto a plate

2 cups flour
1 cup sugar

2 eggs
Instructions
1) Mix the dry ingredients together in a bowl until combined
2) Beat in the eggs one at a time and stir well after each one
3) Pour into a pan and bake at 350 degrees for thirty minutes
4) Let it cool completely before you slice and serve it to everyone
5) Store any leftovers covered at room temperature for a day or two

Ingredients
½ cup butter
¼ cup sugar
⅓ cup honey
2 eggs
Method
1. Cream the butter and sugar together until the mixture is light
2. Add the honey and beat until smooth and well incorporated
3. Add the eggs and mix thoroughly so there are no streaks left
4. Spread in a buttered dish and bake until golden on the top
5. Cool before cutting into squares and serving with the tea
Yield sixteen small squares that keep for about four days
Serves a crowd of hungry children after school on a cold day
